title: Reward Model Interpretability via Optimal and Pessimal Tokens
findings: The study found that certain reward models exhibit a 'linguistic erasure effect,' systematically devaluing religious identity tokens. For example, the tokens 'Jews' and 'jewish' appeared among the lowest-scoring (pessimal) responses for both positive ('greatest thing') and negative ('worst thing') prompts in some models. Other devalued religious terms included 'Muslims' and 'Hezbollah'. This devaluation is theorized to be an unintended bias resulting from harmlessness training objectives.
